classification.difficultyReason: Find intersections by equating expressions and solving quadratics, including vertical lines and tangency.

content.prompt: Find the points of intersection for these lines and parabolas.

spec.description: Unticked common axes with arrows at both ends, blue upward parabola and red horizontal line. No grid, numerical labels or intersection annotations. Viewport is an authored schematic choice because source axis ranges are unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: Parabola y=x^2+x, vertex (-1/2,-1/4), and line y=6; two intersections. Blue and red distinguish the two functions.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curves remain visible in Questions; coordinate answers are excluded.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+x&=6\\x^2+x-6&=0\\(x+3)(x-2)&=0\\x&=-3\text{ or }2\\y&=6\end{align*}$$
The points of intersection are $(-3,6)$ and $(2,6)$.

spec.description: Unticked common axes with arrows at both ends, blue upward parabola and red vertical line. No grid, numerical labels or intersection annotations. Viewport is an authored schematic choice because source axis ranges are unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: Parabola y=x^2-3x, vertex (3/2,-9/4), and vertical line x=1. Their unique intersection lies below the x-axis on the left branch.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curves remain visible in Questions; coordinate answer is excluded.

answer.worked:
Substitute $x=1$ into the parabola:
$$\begin{align*}y&=1^2-3(1)\\y&=-2\end{align*}$$
The point of intersection is $(1,-2)$.

spec.description: Unticked common axes with arrows at both ends, blue upward parabola and red rising line. No grid, numerical labels or intersection annotations. Viewport is an authored schematic choice because source axis ranges are unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: Parabola y=x^2 and line y=3x. Both pass through the origin, which is the parabola's vertex; the second intersection is on the positive branch.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curves remain visible in Questions; coordinate answers are excluded.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=3x\\x^2-3x&=0\\x(x-3)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }3\end{align*}$$
For $x=0$, $y=3(0)=0$. For $x=3$, $y=3(3)=9$.
The points of intersection are $(0,0)$ and $(3,9)$.

spec.description: Unticked common axes with arrows at both ends, blue upward parabola above the x-axis and red falling tangent. No grid, numerical labels or intersection annotations. Viewport is an authored schematic choice because source axis ranges are unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: Parabola y=x^2-3x+5, vertex (3/2,11/4), and line y=-x+4. Tangency at (1,3) is on the left branch.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curves remain visible in Questions; coordinate answer is excluded.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2-3x+5&=-x+4\\x^2-2x+1&=0\\(x-1)^2&=0\\x&=1\\y&=-1+4=3\end{align*}$$
The only point of intersection is $(1,3)$; the line is tangent to the parabola.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}-x^2-4x+3&=2x+12\\x^2+6x+9&=0\\(x+3)^2&=0\\x&=-3\\y&=2(-3)+12=6\end{align*}$$
The only point of intersection is $(-3,6)$; the line is tangent to the parabola.
